title: RePo: Language Models with Context Re-Positioning
claim: Inserting a learned module that assigns context-dependent positions replaces rigid linear indices, letting attention follow the input's intrinsic structure.
layout: 2 stacked panels, bottom-to-top flow, dashed divider, numeric positions above tokens
description: The figure has two stacked panels separated by a dashed line. The bottom panel is the 'Vanilla Layer'. It shows the tokens 'Reverse A B C D : D C B A' with a bold arrow pointing up to rigid integer positions 0 to 9, which run in a black-to-light-blue gradient. Above the positions sit blue 'Self-Attention w/ Position Encoding' and 'MLP' boxes. The top panel, 'Layer with RePo', has the same blue boxes. An orange 'RePo (Pos. Repr. + Assign.)' box sits under the assigned positions, which are fractional and non-monotonic: 0.1, 1.3, 2.7, 3.5, 4.4, 5.8, 4.3, 3.6, 2.6, 1.4. The red 'Assigned Positions' label stands out against the black 'Rigid Positions' label. The reversal task makes the mirrored positions easy to see.
caption: Illustration of the differences between REPO and the vanilla method using the reversal task (Appendix C). The positional encoding can be any standard method (e.g., RoPE, ALiBi). All layers take the hidden states of the token sequence as input.
abstract: In-context learning is fundamental to modern Large Language Models (LLMs); however, prevailing architectures impose a rigid and fixed contextual structure by assigning linear or constant positional indices. The rigid position information poses the full burden of organizing the input structure to attention layers, thus reducing the amount of attention that could be allocated for more critical information. To address this, we propose RePo, a novel mechanism that alleviates the burden for attention layers via context re-positioning. Unlike conventional approaches, RePo utilizes a differentiable module, $f_Ï$, to assign token positions that capture contextual dependencies, rather than replying on pre-defined order. By continually pre-training on the OLMo-2 1B \& 7B models, we demonstrate that RePo consistently enhances performance on tasks involving noisy contexts, structured data, and longer context length, while maintaining competitive performance on general short-context tasks. Analysis reveals that RePo successfully allocates more attention mass to distant but relevant information, assigns positions in a dense and non-linear space, and captures the intrinsic structure of the input context. Our code is at https://github.com/SakanaAI/repo.
